title: Kanda Poha with Roasted Peanuts

steps.text: Place 90g thick poha in a colander and rinse gently under slow running water for 20 seconds; drain completely and let rest 5 minutes.
steps.tip: ⚠️ Where this goes wrong: Rinsing poha for too long or soaking it in standing water turns it into soggy mush. A quick 20-second rinse in a colander is all it takes.

steps.text: Finely chop 1 medium onion (60g) and slice 1 green chilli into thin rounds.
Heat 10ml cooking oil in a pan on medium induction heat (level 4 / 600W) for 45 seconds.
Add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds and sliced green chilli; sauté for 30 seconds until seeds begin to crackle.
Add the chopped onions and sauté for 2.5 minutes until translucent and soft.
Lower heat to minimum, add 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp salt, and the drained poha. Gently toss with a flat spatula for 2 minutes until evenly yellow.
Turn off heat, cover pan with lid for 1 minute to let residual steam plump the flakes, then squeeze 1/2 fresh lemon.
In 1 tsp oil, fry 25g raw peanuts for 2 minutes until crunchy and golden brown; scatter over the warm poha.

title: Moong Dal Khichdi with Desi Ghee Jeera Tadka

steps.text: Measure 60g rice and 60g moong dal together; wash 3 times until water runs mostly clear, then drain.

steps.text: In your kettle or deep pot, melt 10ml desi ghee on medium heat for 45 seconds.
Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1 tsp finely grated ginger; sauté for 30 seconds until warm and fragrant.
Tip in the drained rice-dal mix, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, and 3/4 tsp salt. Stir gently for 1 minute to toast in ghee.
Pour in 500ml water. Cover with lid loosely and simmer on low for 12 minutes until grains are completely soft.
Beat lightly with the back of a ladle to achieve that classic creamy, soupy consistency.
Heat an extra 10ml desi ghee with 1/2 tsp cumin seeds until dark golden, and pour the crackling tadka right on top.

steps.tip: ⚠️ Where this goes wrong: Stirring peanut butter into rolling boiling milk causes the oil to separate and curdle. Turn off heat first, then stir in peanut butter until it melts into silky cream.

steps.text: Pour in 160ml milk (or 80ml milk + 80ml water) and a tiny pinch of salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer on medium-low heat, stirring with a spoon to prevent milk from scorching.
Cook for 2.5 minutes until oats thicken and absorb the milk.
Turn off heat completely. Add 25g peanut butter.
Stir vigorously for 40 seconds until peanut butter melts into velvety, creamy oats.
Pour into a bowl and let settle for 1 minute before topping.
Dollop 45g cold Greek yogurt in the center and swirl into the warm oats for a protein boost.

title: Greek Yogurt Parfait with Crunchy Toasted Granola

steps.text: Take a clean tall glass or broad bowl.
steps.tip: ⚠️ Where this goes wrong: Assembling the parfait hours before eating turns crispy granola soggy and chewy. Keep granola separate and layer on immediately before eating.

steps.text: Spoon 60g chilled, thick Greek yogurt into the base as the first layer.
Slice 1/2 banana into thin coins and place half the slices over the yogurt.
Sprinkle 20g crunchy granola evenly across the fruit layer.
Spoon remaining 60g Greek yogurt on top to form the second layer.
Finish with remaining banana slices and 15g granola.

title: Avocado Sourdough Toast with Sunny-Side Fried Egg

steps.text: Heat a dry skillet or pan on medium induction heat (600W) for 1 minute.
steps.tip: ⚠️ Where this goes wrong: Mashing warm avocado or spreading it on steaming soft bread makes toast limp and wet. Toast bread until rock-crisp, let steam vent 30s, then spread.

steps.text: Spread 8g butter on both sides of 1 thick slice of artisan sourdough bread.
Toast in the pan for 2 minutes per side until golden brown and audibly crispy.
Cut 1/2 ripe avocado, scoop flesh into a small bowl, add 1 tsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp salt, and black pepper.
Mash with a fork to a chunky, spreadable texture.
Generously spread seasoned avocado over the crispy sourdough toast from edge to edge.
Fry 1 egg in butter for 2.5 minutes until whites set and yolk is runny; place atop avocado.
